notes: Idol for LiteRT (litert-community/Idol main 4ce77622, last modified 2026-11-09T17:09:05.000Z): speridlabs/idol (Apache-2.0) with the speridlabs/idol-turbo LoRA (5 steps, no guidance) turns one photo of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat; this form makes 65,536 Gaussians (2,048 anchors; the author's default is 262,144). It is the repo's default form, in its root; the repo's 262k/ folder holds the first release's form (262,144 Gaussians, a graph per block, GPU FP16 with fp32 accumulation), which this record does not cover. Raw LiteRT graphs exported with litert-torch: BiRefNet background removal (bir, CPU), the DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 image encoder (dino_0..3, in litert-community/DINOv3-ViT-H16plus-Idol-LiteRT main e7842b44, gated), the FLUX.2 VAE encoder (vae_0..3, vae_attn, vae_4), the denoiser (den_ctx, den_in, den_joint_00, den_joint_mid for joint blocks 1-22, den_joint_23), the octree decoder (oct, 5 signatures by row count) and the Gaussian decoder (gs_0, gs_mid for graphs 1-6, gs_7). den_joint_mid and gs_mid are one graph each for blocks of the same shape: before each call the app copies that block's float32 weights from den_joint_w.f32 / gs_w.f32 into the graph's weight inputs, so each is compiled once per photo. A pipeline record: `artifact` is manifest.json, which the app opens; it names the 20 graphs with file, bytes, sha256, accelerator and GPU precision (FP16 for the 19 GPU graphs). Identity: every graph's sha256 in manifest.json equals its Hub LFS sha256 (the 16 graphs of litert-community/Idol and the 4 DINOv3 graphs), manifest.json's git blob id and every side and JSON file equal the uploaded files, and the app's install script checks each file's SHA-256 on the phone. Lines, fixed before the first run: (a) each part against the author's PyTorch pipeline (float32, CPU) on the same input, cosine >= 0.99 per compared tensor (the octree and Gaussian decoders against the author's pipeline at 65,536 Gaussians); (b) the whole pipeline's 4-view render PSNR against the author's default (262,144 Gaussians) >= 25 dB on three inputs (nb-armchair and fig-axolotl from the author's gallery, a Pexels photo of a succulent). A pipeline check, so output_match stays null and the scores are metrics; latency_p50_ms stays null and the photo walls are metrics (first_photo_wall_s is the conversion's published speed figure for this phone). Harness: the sample app idol, a debug build of the repo's android/ folder, in its autorun mode: the app starts, compiles 1 graph before the photo, then makes one photo of nb-armchair from the app's files (plan e2e_cool, run 0). Before it the run waited for a cool phone: GPU clock cap 1,300 MHz and thermal status <= 1 in three reads 10 s apart (25 s of waiting; status 0 at the photo's start). While the app ran the GPU clock cap fell to 500 MHz (thermal status 0 -> 2). Not rows here: the parity plan that dumps line (a)'s tensors; the fig-axolotl photo later in the same device run and the succulent photo of a later device run (their PSNR is in metrics); the four photos of the next device run on the warm phone (warm_photo*_wall_s); the repo's first form (262,144 Gaussians, a graph per block, FP16 with fp32 accumulation, in its 262k/ folder) and the other forms measured for the conversion's speed comparison.
quantization: none: the graphs store float32 weights (the shared graphs den_joint_mid and gs_mid get their blocks' float32 weights from den_joint_w.f32 / gs_w.f32 as inputs); every graph but BiRefNet runs on the GPU at GpuOptions precision FP16 (fp16 arithmetic), BiRefNet on the CPU in float32
